newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snecma may drop out of GE90 project - paper.
newsitem.headline: Snecma may drop out of GE90 project - paper.

text.p: The chairman of French aero-engine maker Snecma, Jean-Paul Bechat, is considering dropping the GE90 project and focus instead on low and medium-thrust engines, newspaper Le Monde reported on Thursday.

"Information of an extremely serious nature was revealed, according to which Snecma would drop its involvement in the three versions of the GE90 large engine being developed with General Electric," it quoted a Snecma board member as saying.
Snecma is developing the GE90 in a joint venture with General Electric for the long-haul Boeing 777.
The report quoted Bechat as saying he had told a board meeting on September 11 why he thought it was desirable to study with GE the conditions for participating in the GE90 development.
"At the current stage of negotiations, no decision has been taken," the report quoted Bechat as saying.
The report said Bechat, named as chairman in June, wants to bring Snecma back to break-even this year and refuses to get involved in projects which do not bring in money.
